summary: Stand up emoji-runtime ↔ factory-order contract suite and circulate canonical fixtures.
context: High Command and Toyfoundry now exchange payloads through the emoji-runtime bridge. We require an automated contract harness that proves the translator and factory adapter stay in lockstep across Level-0 templates before propagating to Toysoldiers theatres.

directives.details: Catalogue Level-0 glyph templates, translator intent fields, and factory-order adapter directives impacted by emoji-runtime promotions. Confirm coverage with Toyfoundry deployment owners.

Create curated emoji chains and expected outcomes capturing success, qualifier drift, signal loops, and multi-outcome rituals. Store fixtures under contract_samples/ with documentation for downstream reuse.

Publish tools/contract_test_runner.py that loads fixtures, exercises the translator/adapter pair, and reports mismatches against expectations. Provide CLI affordances for individual case runs and fail-fast operation.
Extend pytest coverage with a contract test module ensuring fixtures run during continuous verification. Document the workflow in README utilities section and brief Toysoldiers/Toyfoundry leads.
Archive evidence in exchange/reports/inbox/order-2025-11-02-043-report.json covering fixtures, runner output, and coordination notes.

success_criteria: Translator outputs for curated chains remain stable across glyph templates
Factory adapter envelopes retain emoji payload provenance and directive telemetry
Contract suite runs via CLI and pytest with zero failures
Fixtures documented for Toyfoundry and Toysoldiers consumption
Completion report logged with evidence and next steps
safety_notes: Keep fixtures lean to minimize maintenance overhead as new glyphs land
If translator interface changes, update factory adapter expectations before promoting to other workspaces
Alert War Office if contract suite identifies regression risk prior to deployment
